summary:
The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda; local legislation governs, and the United Kingdom measures could be applied only by Order in Council.

Bermuda decriminalised consensual sex between adult men in 1994, when the House of Assembly voted 22–16 to strike two sections of the Criminal Code. In July 2013 the Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act, which outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and, in the same instrument, on grounds of age; same-sex marriage was not permitted at that time.

Same-sex couples married in Bermuda in 2017 lost that route the following year. The Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018, replacing same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships available to same-sex and opposite-sex couples alike, which made Bermuda the first jurisdiction anywhere to revoke marriage equality. In March 2022 the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council upheld that restoration of the opposite-sex definition of marriage, so a partnership rather than a marriage is the status available to same-sex couples.

For a transgender visitor the decisive fact is the protection gap. Bermuda has no legal recognition of transgender people and no gender-recognition framework, so there is no route to amend a gender marker on local documents and no recognition machinery a visitor could rely on at the border or in dealings with local authorities. The 2013 amendment's protected ground as enacted is sexual orientation; the inventory does not record gender identity as a protected ground, and no hate-crime provision covering gender identity is sourced here.
tangentialFactors:
Organised religious hostility shapes the social climate for visible same-sex couples. In July the AME church and other congregations protested a Norwegian Dawn cruise sailing to Bermuda as incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre, and the Christian Coalition staged marches against the 1994 decriminalisation vote, with religious leaders publicly divided over the debate.

Bermuda sits in a small group of jurisdictions that have withdrawn a marriage right after granting it, and the 2022 Privy Council ruling confirms that the withdrawal is settled rather than provisional. Visitors should expect partnership-based rights, not marital ones, in any interaction that turns on relationship status.
localsOnly:
Residents may register a domestic partnership, a status open to same-sex and opposite-sex couples alike, following the Governor's assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018. Marriage remains restricted to opposite-sex couples under the definition upheld by the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in March 2022.

The Human Rights Amendment Act of 2013 gives residents a discrimination remedy on the grounds of sexual orientation and age. Transgender residents have no statutory route to legal recognition of their gender identity, and the sourced record does not establish gender identity as a protected ground or a hate-crime category.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether gender identity functions as a protected ground under Bermuda's human-rights legislation, whether any local gender-recognition statute exists, and whether hate-crime provisions reach conduct motivated by gender identity are all unresolved on the present inventory; none of these points is sourced here.

The enforcement record of the 2013 discrimination protections, including complaint volumes and outcomes, is not sourced. Whether the United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 or its 2025 single-sex-services code has ever been proposed for extension to Bermuda by Order in Council is likewise unresolved.
